title: Converge runtime profiles for tokens/sec & p95 regression gate
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our nightly load harness produces noisy tokens/sec and p95 measurements across runners because the test matrix allows many uncontrolled permutations of GPU driver versions, CUDA minor releases, and ephemeral runner images. This noise masks real regressions and leads to false positives in alerts.

Goal: Produce a deterministic, auditable runner/image/driver matrix that (1) reduces variance in tokens/sec and p95 to <5% for stable workloads, (2) enables a regression gate that blocks rollouts when tokens/sec drops >7% or p95 increases >20% for a pinned profile, and (3) surfaces environmental delta causes (e.g., driver vs image).

Scope: Standardize the canonical test profiles (named: stable-x86, stable-ampere, legacy-ampere), pin driver/CUDA combinations for each profile, publish immutable container image SHAs, and update CI/harness to run the canonical matrix nightly and on PRs that touch runtime or runner config. Add automatic attribution in alerting so triage can tell "regression due to image" vs "model/kernel change".

Out-of-scope: Full automatic upgrade strategy for all customer images; we will propose a minor-patch auto-accept later.

Acceptance criteria (must be met to close):
- A documented canonical matrix with driver and CUDA pins in the repo: /infra/bench/matrix.yml (committed).
- CI job 'bench:matrix-stable' runs nightly and on runtime rollouts, producing a reproducible tokens/sec and p95 report with run metadata (git SHA, image SHA, driver version, host kernel).
- Baseline runs for three representative workloads (chat-1k, prompt-512, embedding-bulk-10k) committed to S3 with checksums and result artifacts linked from the test job.
- Regression gate implemented: PRs touching runtime or runner config are blocked if the new PR run shows >7% tokens/sec degradation or >20% p95 regression against baseline for the same canonical profile.
- Alerting to #infra-bench with attribution links and a dashboard panel (Grafana) showing baseline vs current; run ids are searchable.

Risks & trade-offs: Pinning reduces fast-moving flexibility for kernel optimizations and emergency security kernel patches. To mitigate, we propose a parallel 'latest-minor' passive profile that runs but does not gate rollouts. Pin decisions must be reviewed quarterly.

Notes on measurement: Use the harness' built-in steady-state detection window (default 60s warmup, 120s measure) for tokens/sec; p95 is collected per-run and aggregated across 5 contiguous runs. Regression detection uses bootstrap CI for significance when variance near thresholds.
comments: 2026-02-11 — Aisha Patel: Draft matrix committed to feature branch 'eng/ENG-49120-matrix'. See draft YML at https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/eng/ENG-49120-matrix/bench/matrix.yml. Initial profiles: stable-x86 (driver 535.86, cuda 12.1), stable-ampere (driver 535.86, cuda 12.1), legacy-ampere (driver 510.47, cuda 11.8).

2026-02-18 — Mateo Ruiz: Run variance analysis against last 30 nightly runs (workloads chat-1k, prompt-512). Observed tokens/sec stdev: 8.3% on unconstrained matrix, 3.9% when pinned to stable-ampere. Attached CSV to S3: s3://redwood-prod/bench/ENG-49120/variance-report.csv.

2026-02-23 — Quinn Zhao (benching): Implemented CI job bench:matrix-stable in .github/workflows/bench-matrix.yml; testing on PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421. The job archives result artifacts to s3://redwood-prod/bench/runs/<run_id>/ and posts a summary comment back to the PR.

2026-02-27 — Security review (Lena Ortiz): Confirmed no new credentials introduced; images are scanned by Clair and results linked from the job. Vulnerable CVEs should block 'latest-minor' profile only, not stable pinned profiles (operational decision).

2026-03-02 — Design (Maya Chen): Dashboard mock for regression gate posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/ENG-49120+Gate+Dashboard. Panel shows tokens/sec delta, p95 delta, and environment diff. UX asks for direct jump-to-run-link.

2026-03-05 — Mateo Ruiz: Edge case discovered — NVidia driver micro-patch (535.86.1) yields 2% tokens/sec improvement on one runner host due to kernel scheduling. Decided to pin to full patch x.y.z (535.86.1) where available and record 'driver_patch' metadata in run artifacts for attribution. Change approved in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284.

2026-03-08 — Aisha Patel: Implemented regression gate logic in CI: compares run metrics to baseline in BenchStore. PR for gate: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-ops/pull/76. Gate currently runs in 'soft' mode (comments only) until 2026-03-20 to collect false-positive stats.

2026-03-10 — Mateo Ruiz: Nightly runs have been stable for 7 days; variance reduced to target (<5%) on stable profiles. We observed one soft-gate trigger (PR #3490) — tokens/sec degraded by 9%; root cause: a change in batching kernel. Incident ticket created: ENG-49412. Investigations link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/bench-results?orgId=1&var-run=2026-03-09-23
Next steps: (1) Continue soft-gate until 2026-03-20, (2) Expand canonical matrix to include an ARM/Graviton profile, (3) Add nightly delta attribution (image vs driver vs kernel) automation.
